```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

R Markdown (and Quarto) render LaTeX math directly, both inline and as
display equations — useful for writing up the statistics behind a model
alongside the code that fits it.

# Inline Math

Wrapping an expression in single dollar signs keeps it inline with text:
the variance of a real-valued variable $X = (X_1, \ldots, X_n)$ is written
right in the sentence like this.

Source:
```
The variance of a real-valued variable $X = (X_1, \ldots, X_n)$ is given by:
```

# Display Math

Double dollar signs (or a `$$...$$` block) center the equation on its own
line:

$$
\text{Var}(X) =
\left[\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n\left(X_i-\frac{1}{n}
\sum_{i=1}^nX_i\right)^2\right]^\frac{1}{2}
$$

Source:
```
$$
\text{Var}(X) =
\left[\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n\left(X_i-\frac{1}{n}
\sum_{i=1}^nX_i\right)^2\right]^\frac{1}{2}
$$
```

# Mixing LaTeX and R

Math and code can sit side by side in the same document — describe a
function mathematically, then define and run it:

$$f(x) = x^3$$

```{r}
cube <- function(x) x^3
cube(3)
```

This is the same LaTeX engine used to render PDF output (via `tinytex`,
set up in Chapter 0), so anything that displays correctly here will also
render correctly in a knitted PDF.
